text.p: These are the leading stories in Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic says the ruling party must accept the oppposition's justified requests to raise the issue of its members' responsibility in constituencies where irregularities had been observed.

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives students from Nis says the country should resolve its problems within its own institutions and the Serbian government should urgently examine local election records submitted by the students.

- The Serbian Chamber of Commerce reaches accord with the federal and republican governments, central bank of Yugoslavia, and firms on global aims of 1997 economic policy -- increase of production and exports accompanied by stable prices and currency and structural changes in the economy.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT will start flights to Sarajevo and Banja Luka in 15 to 20 days says director Zika Petrovic.

- Serbian parliament adopts law on pension and disability insurance, amendment to the law on social protection and others. Deputies of parties members of the Zajedno coalition boycotted the session because of local election annullments.
- Rally of support for Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic held in Majdanpek.
- Belgraders continue protests over annulled election results. Protests continue in other towns, Kragujevac, Nis.
- OSCE mission to examine records of local elections in Serbia to arrive on December 25.

- Heads of Montenegro's Democratic Party of Socialist, Momir Bulatovic, Milo Djukanovic and Svetozar Marovic sue Montenegrin opposition leaders of National Unity coalition for insulting them at public political gatherings.
